subject.auditScope: Internal self-audit with Agency Chain Map section for AGS v1.6.0 development.

executiveSummary: The AGS self-audit agency chain demonstrates human project authority, non-accusatory audit policy, local implementation boundaries, Runtime Binding and Receipts package evidence, and Governance Memory package evidence. Watch items remain around public-source review, evidence locker design, external third-party audit, and the new foundational status of the agency-chain mapper.

findings.title: Agency chain mapper is foundational
findings.summary: The Agency Chain Mapper is now present, but it is a new local deterministic foundation.
findings.observation: The mapper can identify broken or weak links in local fixtures. It has not yet been connected to an evidence locker or third-party audit workflow.
findings.whyItMatters: Agency-chain evidence should become durable and independently reviewable before external reliance.
auditQuestions: Which agency-chain links are supported by durable evidence artifacts?
Which future workflows should connect chain links to an evidence locker?
recommendedRemediations: Add evidence locker design before external-facing agency-chain reviews.
Expand agency-chain examples into fixture-backed review workflows.

agencyChain.description: Internal self-audit chain showing where AGS preserves human authority, policy constraints, runtime binding package evidence, receipt package evidence, and governance memory package evidence.

links.label: Founder/operator project authority
links.description: Founder/operator defines project scope and can stop, refuse, revise, halt, or escalate release work.

links.label: Audit-core limitations and non-accusatory language
links.description: Audit-core includes limitations, methodology, and non-accusatory report language.

links.label: Prohibited language and no runtime-change posture
links.description: Prohibited language checks and release constraints preserve report posture; runtime spine behavior remains unchanged.

links.label: Codex implementation assistant
links.description: Agents help build but do not own final project authority.

links.label: Local repository edit and test tools
links.description: Tool access is local to repository edits and deterministic verification.

links.label: Release process reviewed through tests and docs
links.description: Proposed release work is reviewed through tests, examples, documentation, and verification commands.

links.label: Human commit/release decision
links.description: Human decides whether to commit or release and can stop, refuse, revise, halt, or escalate.

links.label: Human review and verification requests
links.description: Human reviews outputs and asks for verification before release.

links.label: Runtime Binding package exists
links.description: Runtime Binding exists as a package for permit-bound execution in governed flows.

links.label: Local deterministic implementation boundary
links.description: This release adds deterministic local packages, examples, docs, and CLI behavior without external execution.

links.label: Receipts package and signed receipt support
links.description: Receipts exist as a package and signed receipt support exists in AAG action gate modules.

links.label: Governance Memory package
links.description: Governance Memory exists for human-reviewed receipt-history recommendations.

selfAuditDisclosure.scopeDisclosure: This report is an internal AGS self-audit with an agency-chain map. It should not be treated as independent external assurance.
strengths: Runtime Binding, Receipts, and Governance Memory packages are represented.
watchItems: Public-source review is not first-class yet.
Evidence locker is not implemented yet.
External third-party audit has not been completed.
Agency Chain Mapper is new and foundational.
selfAuditDisclosure.nonCertificationStatement: This self-audit does not claim AGS is enterprise certified, legally compliant, regulator-approved, or production-guaranteed.
